newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian coffee exports seen rising in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian coffee exports seen rising in 1996/97.

text.p: Bolstered by reforms, Ethiopia's coffee exports will rise marginally in 1996/97 (October/September) to 108,000 tonnes from 102,000 tonnes in 1995/96, officials forecast on Thursday.

"Ethiopia shall strive to export up to 108,000 tonnes of its arabica coffee, famed for its aroma and flavour, in the 1996/97 year," Tsegaye Berhane, General Manager of Ethiopian Coffee and Tea Authority, told Reuters in an interview.

Ethiopia exported 102,000 tonnes of coffee 1995/96, the highest exported volume in its trade history. But it earned only $279.5 million from those efforts, lower than the $300.9 million it received for exporting 78,420 tonnes of coffee in 1994/95.
The Ethiopian Coffee and Tea Authority is a government agency that oversees crop production and marketing.

"We must strive not only to increase the volume of our coffee exports but it is most essential that the commodity should be of the highest quality to compete among the best in the world," Tsegaye said.
Ethiopia is Africa's third largest producer of coffee after Uganda and Ivory Coast. Coffee is its main export commodity and accounts for about 60 percent of its foreign exchange revenues.
Tsegaye said Ethiopia's coffee exports during previous years had been very low.
Much of Ethiopia's coffee is still consumed locally and Tsegaye said any change in drinking habits to more tea would allow the country to increase its coffee exports.
Ethiopia's annual coffee production has jumped to around 300,000 tonnes from 250,000 tonnes previously.
Tsegaye said some coffee exporters opted to sell coffee destined for export on the local market, which undermined efforts to promote coffee exports.

Private players are now dominant in an Ethiopian coffee market previously monopolised by the government and previously poorly managed under the Marxist rule of Mengistu Haile Mariam, the dictator ousted in May 1991.
